Validate ForgeOS agent, Skill, profile, permission, reference, structural-test, and real read-only delegation behavior before a first software-project pilot.

ForgeOS integration audit completed: 16 agent TOMLs, 13 discovered Skills, 8 catalog profiles, references, permissions, and structural tests passed; real read-only Architect delegation passed, Frontend-to-Reviewer delegation was partial due an unresolved rejected-promise contract, and Release Manager delegation failed because the expected seventeenth subagent is not installed. No configuration correction was made; ForgeOS is not ready for an end-to-end pilot until the missing release capability and dynamic instantiation gaps are resolved.

Finalizing ForgeOS integration by adding the seventeenth subagent, Release Manager, three non-overlapping release Skills, structural coverage, a read-only release delegation simulation, Scenario B contract analysis, and centralized validation evidence.

Release Manager and three non-overlapping release Skills integrated; 17 agent TOMLs and 16 Skill manifests validated. Scenario B remains PARTIAL because no application implementation exists, but its save rejection contract and required tests are explicit. Scenario C used a real Release Manager in a fresh read-only Codex session and correctly returned blocked for missing Git history, changelog, artifacts, and release evidence without sensitive actions. Bootstrap and one structural test pass; ForgeOS is ready for a controlled first pilot, not for production release.

ForgeOS now uses the canonical AGENTS.md root instructions and canonical SKILL.md manifests exclusively; lowercase fallback references were removed from active configuration, documentation, conventions, and structural validation. Bootstrap and the structural test pass.

Adding a generated Claude Code adapter while preserving Codex: CLAUDE.md imports canonical governance, Claude agents derive from the 17 Codex role sources, Claude Skills mirror the shared Skill sources, and project settings add explicit permission gates.

Claude Code adapter integrated without changing canonical Codex role or Skill sources: 17 generated native agents and 16 mirrored Skills validate against their canonical sources; project settings and documentation pass structural tests and Claude doctor. Claude CLI discovers all 17 ForgeOS agents, but model and dynamic Skill execution remain unverified because local OAuth is expired.

Building a Python-standard-library ForgeOS installer for isolated global or local Codex and Claude Code installations on Windows, macOS, and Linux, with explicit conflict handling, ownership manifests, safe updates and uninstalls, complete documentation, and temporary-directory tests.

ForgeOS now has a Python-standard-library installer with install, update, status, and uninstall for local or global Codex, Claude, or combined targets; ownership manifests, explicit conflict backups, transactional updates, traversal protection, drift preservation, opt-in settings, and isolated lifecycle tests. Documentation, bootstrap validation, adapter synchronization, and independent review pass; native execution remains verified on Windows only.

Preparing the first v0.1.0 release on a new local dev branch: verified changelog, Git and release procedure, full structural and installer validation, independent review, and an explicit stop before merge, tag, push, or GitHub publication pending user authorization.

The local dev candidate documents v0.1.0, its verified scope, limitations, Git workflow, release gates, branch-protection recommendations, and recovery rules. Structural, adapter, installer, whitespace, sensitive-filename, and independent review gates pass; merge, tag, push, pull request, GitHub protection verification, and release publication remain pending explicit authorization and authenticated GitHub access.
